facts.t: The arbitrator decides, the conciliator suggests, the mediator listens
facts.d: Three roles on a single spectrum. Arbitration is adjudicatory and produces a binding award; conciliation is advisory and proposes terms; mediation is purely facilitative and cannot impose anything at all.
Arbitrator fees, venue costs and full legal representation make it the costliest of the three. Mediation is usually the cheapest — mediator fees plus, at most, court fees for enforcement.

facts.t: A conciliation settlement is treated as an arbitral award
facts.d: Under section 73 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, a signed conciliation settlement carries the same status as an award — which is why there is no appeal against it.

bank.q: Which of the three processes involves an adjudicatory role for the neutral?
bank.e: Arbitration alone. Conciliation is advisory and mediation facilitative.

bank.q: With reference to time frames, consider the following statements:
s: Arbitration must conclude within twelve months of completion of pleadings, extendable by six.
Mediation must conclude within 120 days, extendable to 180.
Conciliation has a statutory limit of ninety days.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Conciliation has no specific statutory limit — the parties agree it.

bank.q: Match List I (process) with List II (enforcement provision):
pairs: 2. Section 36 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act
3. Section 73 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act
bank.e: Section 36 for awards, 73 for conciliation settlements, 28 for mediated settlements, and 21 for mediation confidentiality.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: A conciliator may propose settlement terms
A mediator may impose a settlement if the parties deadlock
A mediated settlement may be challenged within ninety days
bank.e: The mediator has no power to impose anything — the process is facilitative by definition.

bank.as: Mediation is described as the most flexible of the three processes.
bank.rs: The parties retain control over both the process and the outcome.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. Arbitration is the least flexible, bound by agreed or institutional rules.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about confidentiality:
s: Section 75 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act bars disclosure in conciliation.
An arbitral award may become public unless the parties agree otherwise.
Mediation confidentiality admits no exceptions whatsoever.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Section 21 of the Mediation Act allows exceptions for implementation and enforcement.

bank.q: An arbitral award may be challenged under section 34 within:
bank.e: Three months, on limited grounds. A mediated settlement may be challenged within ninety days under section 29 of the Mediation Act.

bank.q: All of the following describe the extent of court involvement correctly EXCEPT:
o: In arbitration, courts assist with appointment, interim measures and enforcement
In conciliation, court involvement is minimal
In mediation, courts may refer cases and enforce settlements
In conciliation, courts conduct a merits review before the settlement takes effect
bank.e: There is no merits review. A signed conciliation settlement takes effect as an arbitral award under section 73.

bank.q: Which process is governed by section 89 of the Code of Civil Procedure among its sources?
bank.e: Mediation, alongside the Mediation Act, 2023 and the Supreme Court Mediation Rules.

bank.q: With reference to the appointment of neutrals, consider the following:
s: Conciliators may number between one and three.
A mediator must be certified under the 2023 Act.
An arbitrator may be appointed by a court where the parties fail to agree.
bank.e: All three are correct — each process has its own appointment architecture.
